```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# load code and libraries
source(file = "00_setup.R")
library(kableExtra)
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)
library(ggside)
library(ggpubr)
library(NCA)

# define directories
dir_out <- file.path(dir_anal, "NCA")
if (!dir.exists(dir_out)) dir.create(dir_out)

# set up chunks
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

# load pre-processed observation data
df_mqi_section <- read.csv(file = file.path(dir_base_obs, "data_MQI_section.csv"))
df_fft_section <- read.csv(file = file.path(dir_base_obs, "data_FFT_section.csv"))

# segment level data
df_mqi_raw <- read.csv(file = file.path(dir_base_obs, "data_MQI_segment.csv"))
df_fft_raw <- read.csv(file = file.path(dir_base_obs, "data_FFT_segment.csv"))

# information about the class sections
load(file.path(dir_data, "da34414-0003_v10_REST.rda"))

# information about teachers
load(file.path(dir_data, "da34414-0002_v10_REST.rda"))

# define columns that contain pupil characteristics
cols_pup <- names(da34414.0003)[grepl("DAD_PERC", names(da34414.0003))]
cols_pup_lbl <- c("% gifted", "% male", "% special education status", "% English language learner status", "% Free or reduced lunch price status", "% Other ethnic background", "% Asian", "% Hispanic", "% Black", "% White", "% disability status")
cols_pup_num <- c("DAD_AVERAGEAGE", "FFT_CEV_adj", "VA_SAM_adj", "VA_BAM_adj")
cols_pup_num <- c("DAD_AVERAGEAGE")
cols_pup_num_lbl <- c("Average age", "Classroom Environment rating (adj.)", 
                      "Value-added state maths test score (adj.)", "Value-added BAM test score (adj.)")
cols_pup_num_lbl <- c("Average age")

# script-level vars
DVs_main <- c("VA_SAM", "VA_BAM")
DVs_supp <- c("VA_NOAGGR_SAM", "VA_NOAGGR_BAM")
DVs <- c(DVs_main, DVs_supp)

# define all VAMs
VAM <- c("VA_SAM", "VA_SAM_std", "VA_SAM_adj", "VA_SAM_adj_std", 
         "VA_NOAGGR_SAM", "VA_NOAGGR_SAM_std", "VA_NOAGGR_SAM_adj", "VA_NOAGGR_SAM_adj_std", 
         "VA_BAM", "VA_BAM_std", "VA_BAM_adj", "VA_BAM_adj_std",
         "VA_NOAGGR_BAM", "VA_NOAGGR_BAM_std", "VA_NOAGGR_BAM_adj", "VA_NOAGGR_BAM_adj_std"
)

# colouring
cols_obs <- c(
  "FFT_CEV" = teal,
  "FFT_CERR" = coral,
  "FFT_ECL" = purple,
  "FFT_MCP" = orange,
  "FFT_MSB" = cyan,
  "FFT_CS" = navy,
  "FFT_UQDT" = red,
  "FFT_ESL" = blue,
  "FFT_INS" = yellow,
  "FFT_UAI" = black
)

cols_pred <- c(
  "MQI_EI" = coral,
  "MQI_SPMMR" = purple,
  "MQI_RICH" = orange,
  "MQI_WWSM" = cyan
)

cols_vam <- c(
  "SAM" = blue,
  "BAM" = red
)

```

```{r fft, results='asis', message=F, eval=F}
# score columns
score_fft <- c(
  "FFT_CERR", # "Creating an Environment of Respect & Rapport" 
  "FFT_ECL", # "Establishing a Culture for Learning" 
  "FFT_MCP", # "Managing Classroom Procedures" 
  "FFT_MSB", # "Managing Student Behaviour" 
  "FFT_CS", # "Communicating with Students" 
  "FFT_UQDT", # "Using Questioning & Discussion Techniques" 
  "FFT_ESL", # "Engaging Students in Learning" 
  "FFT_UAI" # "Using Assessment in Instruction" 
)
score_fft <- score_fft[1:4]

# assign labels
label_fft <- c(
  "Creating an environment of respect and rapport", 
  "Establishing a culture for learning", 
  "Managing classroom procedures", 
  "Managing student behaviour", 
  "Communicating with students", 
  "Using questioning and discussion techniques", 
  "Engaging students in learning", 
  "Using assessment in instruction" 
)
label_fft <- label_fft[1:4]

# assign domains
domain_fft <- c(
  rep("Classroom environment (FFT_CEV)", 4),
  rep("Instruction (FFT_INS)", 4)
)
domain_fft <- domain_fft[1:4]

# markdown table to map item name and description
instrument_fft <- data.frame(Item = score_fft, Description = label_fft, Domain = domain_fft)
instrument_fft %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), fixed_thead = T, full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  print()

# define scale
scale_fft <- c(
  "1:\nUnsatisfactory",
  "2:\nBasic",
  "3:\nProficient",
  "4:\nDistinguished"
)

# plotting params
cols_fft <- c("1 - Unsatisfactory" = purple, "2 - Basic" = blue, "3 - Proficient" = red, "4 - Distinguished" = teal, "NA" = navy)
names(cols_fft) <- c(scale_fft, "NA")
levels_fft <- c("4", "3", "2", "1")

```

```{r mqi, results='asis', message=F, eval=F}
# score columns
score_mqi <- c(
  "MQI_EI", # "Errors & Imprecision"
  "MQI_RICH", # "Richness"
  "MQI_WWSM", # "Working With Students & Mathematics"
  # "MQI_CWCM", # "Classroom Work Connected to Mathematics" # grade dependent
  # "MQI_ET", # "Explicitness and Thoroughness" # grade dependent
  "MQI_SPMMR" # "Student Participation in Meaning Making & Reasoning"
)

# assign labels
label_mqi <- c(
  "Errors and imprecision", 
  "Richness", 
  "Working With students and mathematics",
  # "Classroom Work Connected to Mathematics", 
  # "Explicitness and Thoroughness", 
  "Student participation in meaning making and reasoning" 
)

# assign domains
domain_mqi <- c(
  "Teacher-content relationship",
  "Teacher-content relationship",
  "Teacher-pupil relationship",
  # "Pupil-content relationship",
  # "Pupil-content relationship",
  "Pupil-content relationship"
)

# markdown table to map item name and description
instrument_mqi <- data.frame(Item = score_mqi, Description = label_mqi, Domain = domain_mqi)
instrument_mqi %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), fixed_thead = T, full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  print()

# define scale
scale_mqi <- c(
  "1: Low/not\npresent",
  "2: Mid/partially\npresent",
  "3: High/predominantly\npresent"
)

# plotting params
cols_mqi <- c("1 - Low/not present" = red, "2 - Mid/partially present" = orange, "3 - High/predominantly present" = teal, "NA" = navy)
names(cols_mqi) <- c(scale_mqi, "NA")
levels_mqi <- c("3", "2", "1")
```


```{r y2, eval=F, include=FALSE}
# define sections in Year 2 for which there is MQI and FFT data and outcome data
sections_y2 <- intersect(da34414.0003$SECTION_ICPSR_ID[!is.na(da34414.0003$VA2011_MATH) & !is.na(da34414.0003$VA2011_BAM) & da34414.0003$VA2011_MATH_N > 1 & da34414.0003$VA2011_BAM_N > 1],
                         intersect(
                           df_mqi_section$SECTION_ICPSR_ID[df_mqi_section$YEAR == 2 & !is.na(df_mqi_section$MQI_EI)],
                           df_fft_section$SECTION_ICPSR_ID[df_fft_section$YEAR == 2 & !is.na(df_fft_section$FFT_CERR)])
)

# combine observation data
classes_y2 <- left_join(
  df_mqi_section %>% 
    filter(SECTION_ICPSR_ID %in% sections_y2)# & TEACHER_ICPSR_ID %in% teachers_both)
  , 
  df_fft_section %>% 
    filter(SECTION_ICPSR_ID %in% sections_y2)# & TEACHER_ICPSR_ID %in% teachers_both)
) 

# add information about the class sections
classes_y2 <- right_join(
  da34414.0003 %>%
    select(DISTRICT_ICPSR_ID, SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID, TEACHER_ICPSR_ID, SECTION_ICPSR_ID, 
           GRADE, SUBJECT, SUBJECTLEVEL, YEAR, RANDOMIZED,
           DAD_NUMSTUDENTS, DAD_PERCGIFTED, DAD_PERCMALE, DAD_PERCSPED, DAD_PERCDISABILITY,
           DAD_PERCELL, DAD_AVERAGEAGE, DAD_PERCFRL, DAD_PERCWHITE, DAD_PERCBLACK, DAD_PERCASIAN, DAD_PERCHISPANIC, DAD_PERCRACEOTHER,
           VA2011_MATH, VA2011_MATH_SE, VA2011_MATH_N, 
           VA2011_NOAGGR_MATH, VA2011_NOAGGR_MATH_SE, VA2011_NOAGGR_MATH_N,
           VA2011_BAM, VA2011_BAM_SE, VA2011_BAM_N, 
           VA2011_NOAGGR_BAM, VA2011_NOAGGR_BAM_SE, VA2011_NOAGGR_BAM_N,
           NUMVIDEOS, FFT_P2_NUMVIDEOS, FFTM_P2_NUMVIDEOS, CLASS_NUMVIDEOS, MQI_P2_NUMVIDEOS) %>%
    mutate(
      GRADE = as.character(GRADE),
      GRADE = as.numeric(substr(GRADE, nchar(GRADE), nchar(GRADE))),
      SUBJECT = as.character(SUBJECT),
      SUBJECT = substr(SUBJECT, 5, nchar(SUBJECT)),
      SUBJECTLEVEL = as.character(SUBJECTLEVEL),
      SUBJECTLEVEL = substr(SUBJECTLEVEL, 5, nchar(SUBJECTLEVEL)),
      YEAR = as.character(YEAR),
      YEAR = as.numeric(substr(YEAR, 5, nchar(YEAR))),
      RANDOMIZED = as.character(RANDOMIZED),
      RANDOMIZED = substr(RANDOMIZED, nchar(RANDOMIZED), nchar(RANDOMIZED))
    ), 
  classes_y2 %>%
    select(-SUBJECT, -GRADE, -YEAR),
  join_by(DISTRICT_ICPSR_ID, SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID, TEACHER_ICPSR_ID, SECTION_ICPSR_ID)) %>% 
  rename(
    VA_SAM = VA2011_MATH,
    VA_SAM_SE = VA2011_MATH_SE,
    VA_SAM_N = VA2011_MATH_N,
    VA_NOAGGR_SAM = VA2011_NOAGGR_MATH,
    VA_NOAGGR_SAM_SE = VA2011_NOAGGR_MATH_SE,
    VA_NOAGGR_SAM_N = VA2011_NOAGGR_MATH_N,
    VA_BAM = VA2011_BAM,
    VA_BAM_SE = VA2011_BAM_SE,
    VA_BAM_N = VA2011_BAM_N,
    VA_NOAGGR_BAM = VA2011_NOAGGR_BAM,
    VA_NOAGGR_BAM_SE = VA2011_NOAGGR_BAM_SE,
    VA_NOAGGR_BAM_N = VA2011_NOAGGR_BAM_N
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

teachers_y2 <- da34414.0002 %>%
  select(contains("_ID") | contains("PRESENTY1") | contains("PRESENTY2") | contains("RANDOMIZED") |  contains("GRADEY2") | contains("SUBJECTY2") | contains("SUBJECTLEVELY2") | contains("DAD_") | contains("NUMSECT_MATH_Y2") | contains("NUMVIDS_MATH_Y2") | contains("NUMSECT_MATHELA_Y2")) %>%
  filter(TEACHER_ICPSR_ID %in% classes_y2$TEACHER_ICPSR_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    # make factor variables numeric
    GRADEY2 = as.numeric(as.character(GRADEY2)),
    SUBJECTY2 = as.character(SUBJECTY2),
    SUBJECTY2 = substr(SUBJECTY2, 5, nchar(SUBJECTY2)),
    SUBJECTLEVELY2 = as.character(SUBJECTLEVELY2)#,
  ) %>% 
  rename(GRADE = GRADEY2,
         SUBJECT = SUBJECTY2,
         SUBJECTLEVEL = SUBJECTLEVELY2,
         NUMSECT_MATH = NUMSECT_MATH_Y2,
         NUMVIDS_MATH = NUMVIDS_MATH_Y2,
         NUMSECT_MATHELA = NUMSECT_MATHELA_Y2) %>%
  relocate(starts_with("NUM"), .after = SUBJECTLEVEL) # %>% select(-DAD_YRSEXP)

# define sections, observation data and teacher data
sections <- unique(classes_y2$SECTION_ICPSR_ID)
df_classes <- classes_y2
df_teachers <- teachers_y2

YEAR <- "Y2_all"
```

```{r preproc, eval=F, message=F}
# --- PROCESS TEACHER LEVEL DATA --- #

df_teachers <- df_teachers %>%
  mutate(
    # make factor variables numeric
    DAD_MALE = as.character(DAD_MALE),
    DAD_MALE = as.numeric(substr(DAD_MALE, nchar(DAD_MALE), nchar(DAD_MALE))),
    DAD_WHITE = as.character(DAD_WHITE),
    DAD_WHITE = as.numeric(substr(DAD_WHITE, nchar(DAD_WHITE), nchar(DAD_WHITE))),
    DAD_BLACK = as.character(DAD_BLACK),
    DAD_BLACK = as.numeric(substr(DAD_BLACK, nchar(DAD_BLACK), nchar(DAD_BLACK))),
    DAD_HISPANIC = as.character(DAD_HISPANIC),
    DAD_HISPANIC = as.numeric(substr(DAD_HISPANIC, nchar(DAD_HISPANIC), nchar(DAD_HISPANIC))),
    DAD_RACEOTHER = as.character(DAD_RACEOTHER),
    DAD_RACEOTHER = as.numeric(substr(DAD_RACEOTHER, nchar(DAD_RACEOTHER), nchar(DAD_RACEOTHER))),
    DAD_MASTERSPLUS = as.character(DAD_MASTERSPLUS),
    DAD_MASTERSPLUS = as.numeric(substr(DAD_MASTERSPLUS, nchar(DAD_MASTERSPLUS), nchar(DAD_MASTERSPLUS))),
    
    DAD_YRSEXP_DIFF = DAD_YRSEXP - DAD_YRSEXPDIST,
    # bucket experience
    DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP <= 18, as.character(ceil_even(DAD_YRSEXP)), "18+"),
    DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL %in% c("0", "2"), "2", DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL),
    DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL = factor(DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL, levels = c("2", "4", "6", "8", "10", "12", "14", "16", "18", "18+")),
    # group experience
    DAD_YRSEXP_GRP = case_when(
      DAD_YRSEXP >= 0 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 2 ~ "[0, 2]", # "New (0-2 yr)",
      DAD_YRSEXP > 2 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 5 ~ "(2, 5]", # "Early career (2-5 yr)",
      DAD_YRSEXP > 5 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 10 ~ "(5, 10]", # "Established (5-10 yr)",
      DAD_YRSEXP > 10 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 20 ~ "(10, 20]", # "Experienced (10-20 yr)"
      DAD_YRSEXP > 20 ~ "(20, Inf)" # "Highly experienced (20+ yr)"
    ),
    DAD_YRSEXP_NEW = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP >= 0 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 2, 1, if_else(is.na(DAD_YRSEXP), NA, 0)),
    DAD_YRSEXP_EARLY = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP > 2 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 5, 1, if_else(is.na(DAD_YRSEXP), NA, 0)),
    DAD_YRSEXP_EST = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP > 5 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 10, 1, if_else(is.na(DAD_YRSEXP), NA, 0)),
    DAD_YRSEXP_EXP = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP > 10 & DAD_YRSEXP <= 20, 1, if_else(is.na(DAD_YRSEXP), NA, 0)),
    DAD_YRSEXP_HIGH = if_else(DAD_YRSEXP > 20, 1, if_else(is.na(DAD_YRSEXP), NA, 0)),
  )

# generate bucket labels

# --- AGGREGATE FROM SECTION TO TEACHER LEVEL --- #

# note: in the context of Y2 data (one section per teacher), this step won't transform the data

# FFT variance decomposition (Table 11)
vd_fft <- data.frame(
  score = c(# DIFFERENT ORDER!!
    "FFT_CERR",  
    "FFT_UQDT",
    "FFT_ECL", 
    "FFT_MCP", 
    "FFT_CS",  
    "FFT_MSB", 
    "FFT_ESL", 
    "FFT_UAI" 
  ),
  teacher = c(30, 15, 25, 24, 21, 33, 20, 18),
  section = c(3, 4, 0, 6, 1, 8, 3, 0),
  lesson = c(8, 12, 10, 0, 2, 1, 12, 3),
  rater = c(7, 6, 7, 7, 8, 3, 6, 9),
  residual = c(53, 62, 57, 62, 68, 54, 59, 70)
)

# MQI variance decomposition (Table 11)
vd_mqi <- data.frame(
  score = score_mqi,
  teacher = c(6, 8, 7, 13),
  section = rep(0, length(score_mqi)),
  lesson = c(5, 24, 25, 27),
  rater = c(16, 10, 13, 11),
  residual = c(74, 58, 55, 49)
)

# combine
vd_obs <- rbind(vd_fft, vd_mqi)

# define all observation scores to aggregate
obs_score <- c(score_fft, score_mqi)

# aggregate
df_obs  <- df_classes %>%
  group_by(DISTRICT_ICPSR_ID, SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID, TEACHER_ICPSR_ID) %>%
  # average rating score
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(obs_score), 
      ~mean_or_na(.x),
      .names = "{.col}"
    ), 
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    # FFT count data
    df_fft_raw %>%
      filter(SECTION_ICPSR_ID %in% sections) %>%
      group_by(DISTRICT_ICPSR_ID, SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID, TEACHER_ICPSR_ID) %>%
      summarise(
        # count scores, unique raters, segments, lessons and sections
        across(
          all_of(gsub("FFT_", "", score_fft)), list(
            N_SCORE = ~sum(!is.na(.x)),
            N_RATER = ~n_distinct(ICPSR_RATER_ID[!is.na(.x)]),
            N_SEGMENT = ~n_distinct(paste0(VIDEO_ICPSR_ID, "_",SEGMENT)[!is.na(.x)]),
            N_LESSON = ~n_distinct(VIDEO_ICPSR_ID[!is.na(.x)]),
            N_SECTION = ~n_distinct(SECTION_ICPSR_ID[!is.na(.x)])
          ), .names = "{fn}_FFT_{.col}"),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    # MQI count data
    df_mqi_raw %>%
      filter(SECTION_ICPSR_ID %in% sections) %>%
      group_by(DISTRICT_ICPSR_ID, SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID, TEACHER_ICPSR_ID) %>%
      summarise(
        # count scores, unique raters, segments, lessons and sections
        across(
          all_of(gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi)), list(
            N_SCORE = ~sum(!is.na(.x)),
            N_RATER = ~n_distinct(ICPSR_RATER_ID[!is.na(.x)]),
            N_SEGMENT = ~n_distinct(paste0(VIDEO_ICPSR_ID, "_",SEGMENT)[!is.na(.x)]),
            N_LESSON = ~n_distinct(VIDEO_ICPSR_ID[!is.na(.x)]),
            N_SECTION = ~n_distinct(SECTION_ICPSR_ID[!is.na(.x)])
          ), .names = "{fn}_MQI_{.col}"),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()


# compute the implied reliability of each score at teacher level
for (i in 1:length(obs_score)) {
  
  # compute reliability
  df_obs[, paste0(obs_score[i], "_rel")] <- met_reliability(
    perc_teacher = vd_obs$teacher[vd_obs$score == obs_score[i]], 
    perc_section = vd_obs$section[vd_obs$score == obs_score[i]], num_section = df_obs[, paste0("N_SECTION_", obs_score[i])], 
    perc_lesson = vd_obs$lesson[vd_obs$score == obs_score[i]], num_lesson = df_obs[, paste0("N_LESSON_", obs_score[i])],
    perc_rater = vd_obs$rater[vd_obs$score == obs_score[i]], num_rater = df_obs[, paste0("N_RATER_", obs_score[i])],
    perc_residual = vd_obs$residual[vd_obs$score == obs_score[i]], num_scores = df_obs[, paste0("N_SCORE_", obs_score[i])]
  )
  
  # apply shrinkage based on reliability
  # adjusted score = MEAN + reliability * (observed score - MEAN)
  df_obs[, paste0(obs_score[i], "_adj")] <- c(mean(df_obs[, obs_score[i]], na.rm = T) + 
                                                df_obs[, paste0(obs_score[i], "_rel")] * scale(df_obs[, obs_score[i]], center = T, scale = F))
  
}

# aggregate domain scores
df_obs$FFT_CEV <- rowMeans(df_obs[, paste0(instrument_fft$Item[grepl("CEV", instrument_fft$Domain)])])

score_fft2 <- c("FFT_CEV", instrument_fft$Item[grepl("CEV", instrument_fft$Domain)])

#     VA_NOAGGR_BAM = weighted.mean(VA_NOAGGR_BAM, w = VA_NOAGGR_BAM_N), 
#     VA_NOAGGR_BAM_adj = weighted.mean(VA_NOAGGR_BAM_adj, w = VA_NOAGGR_BAM_N), 
#     .groups = "drop")

# NOTE: because VAMs were computed within grades and districts rather than across the sample, any differences between groups have already been removed

df_vam <- df_classes %>%
  mutate( # convert SE to SD
    across(all_of(DVs),
           ~get(paste0(cur_column(), "_SE")) * sqrt(get(paste0(cur_column(), "_N"))),
           .names = "{.col}_SD")
  ) %>%
  group_by(DISTRICT_ICPSR_ID, SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID, TEACHER_ICPSR_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(DVs),
           ~weighted.mean(.x, w = get(paste0(cur_column(), "_N"))),
           .names = "{.col}"),
    across(all_of(DVs),
           .fns = list(
             # combined SE as DV_SE
             SE = ~{
               ns <- get(paste0(cur_column(), "_N"))
               sds <- get(paste0(cur_column(), "_SD"))
               total_n <- sum(ns)
               pooled_var <- sum((ns-1) * sds^2) / (total_n - sum(!is.na(ns)))
               sqrt(pooled_var / total_n)
             },
             # SECTIONS = ~n(),
             # Total N as DV_N
             N = ~sum(get(paste0(cur_column(), "_N")))
           ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# apply shrinkage based on reliability
for (i in 1:length(DVs)) {
  
  # estimate reliability
  df_vam[, paste0(DVs[i], "_rel")] <- vam_reliability(vam = df_vam[, paste0(DVs[i])], se = df_vam[, paste0(DVs[i], "_SE")])
  
  # adjusted score = MEAN + reliability * (observed score - MEAN)
  df_vam[, paste0(DVs[i], "_adj")] <- c(mean(df_vam[, DVs[i]], na.rm = T) + df_vam[, paste0(DVs[i], "_rel")] * scale(df_vam[, DVs[i]], center = T, scale = F))
  
}


# combine
df_teachers <- df_teachers %>%
  left_join(df_obs) %>%
  left_join(df_vam) %>%
  as.data.frame()
rm(df_obs, df_vam)

# standardise scores
scores <- c(score_fft2, score_mqi, DVs)
for (i in 1:length(scores)) {
  
  df_teachers[, paste0(scores[i], "_std")] <- c(scale(df_teachers[, paste0(scores[i])], center = T, scale = T))
  df_teachers[, paste0(scores[i], "_adj_std")] <- c(scale(df_teachers[, paste0(scores[i], "_adj")], center = T, scale = T))
  
}

cols_teach <- cols_teach[!grepl("YRSEXPDIST", cols_teach)]
cols_teach <- setdiff(cols_teach, c("DAD_YRSEXP", "DAD_YRSEXP_GRP", "DAD_YRSEXP_CEIL", "DAD_YRSEXP_DIFF"))

# define columns that contain numerical teacher characteristics
cols_teach_num <- c("DAD_YRSEXP", 
                    # "DAD_YRSEXPDIST", "DAD_YRSEXP_DIFF", 
                    # "FFT_CEV_adj", "VA_SAM_adj", "VA_BAM_adj"
                    paste0(scores, "_adj")
)
```

```{r demogs_teachers, results='asis', eval=F, message=F}
                      y = ys[i],
                      cor = cor$estimate,
                      ci_l = cor$conf.int[1],
                      ci_u = cor$conf.int[2],
                      df = cor$parameter,
                      t = cor$statistic,
                      p = cor$p.value,
                      N = sum(!is.na(df_teachers[, xs[j]]))
    )
    
    if (i == 1 & j == 1) df_cor <- cor else df_cor <- bind_rows(df_cor, cor)
  }
}

                   group_by(SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID) %>%
                   summarise(
                     across(all_of(paste0(c(score_fft2[1], DVs_main), "_adj")), ~mean(.x, na.rm = T))
                   ) %>%
                   tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(paste0(c(score_fft2[1], DVs_main), "_adj")), names_to = "Domain", values_to = "School_mean"),
                 df_teachers %>%
                   group_by(SCHOOL_ICPSR_ID) %>%
                   summarise(
                     across(all_of(paste0(c(score_fft2[1], DVs_main), "_adj")), ~sd(.x, na.rm = T))
                   ) %>%
                   tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(paste0(c(score_fft2[1], DVs_main), "_adj")), names_to = "Domain", values_to = "School_sd")) %>%
  ungroup() 

# add to markdown
tmp %>% 
  group_by(Domain) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_within_sd = mean(School_sd, na.rm = T), # SD is NA when there is only one section per school
    within_var = mean(School_sd^2, na.rm = T)
  ) %>% 
  right_join(tmp %>% 
               group_by(Domain) %>%
               summarise(
                 between_sd = sd(School_mean, na.rm = T),
                 between_var = between_sd^2)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_var = within_var + between_var,
    within_pct = within_var / total_var,
    between_pct = between_var / total_var
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = "Within vs between school variation - teacher level", digits = 3, row.names = F) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), fixed_thead = T, full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  add_footnote(paste0("Note. Data is available for ", nrow(df_teachers), " Teachers avg_within_sd is the average within-school SD. between_sd is the SD of school means. Classrooms were aggregated at teacher-level before aggregating at school level."), notation = "none")
```

```{r adj_sum, eval = F, warning = F, results='asis'}
# --- describe how observation scores shift --- #

# compute adjusted scale start and end point
tmp <-
  df_teachers %>%
  # RELIABILITY
  summarise(
    across(
      ends_with("_rel") & ! starts_with("VA_"),
      ~mean(.x), .names = "{gsub('_rel', '', .col)}"
    )
  ) %>%
  bind_rows(
    df_teachers %>%
      # SAMPLE MEAN AND SD
      summarise(
        across(
          all_of(c(score_fft, score_mqi)),
          ~mean(.x)
        )
      )
  ) %>%
  bind_rows(
    df_teachers %>%
      # MINIMUM SCALE VALUE
      summarise(
        across(
          all_of(c(score_fft, score_mqi)),
          ~if(grepl("FFT", cur_column())) 1 else if (grepl("MQI", cur_column())) 1 else NA
        )
      )
  ) %>%
  bind_rows(
    df_teachers %>%
      # MAXIMUM SCALE VALUE
      summarise(
        across(
          all_of(c(score_fft, score_mqi)),
          ~if(grepl("FFT", cur_column())) 4 else if (grepl("MQI", cur_column())) 3 else NA
        )
      )
  ) %>%
  {
    # adjusted min value
    # MEAN + RELIABILITY * (MIN_RATING - MEAN)
    adjusted_row <- .[2, ] + .[1, ] * (.[3, ] - .[2, ])
    bind_rows(., adjusted_row)
  } %>%
  {
    # adjusted max value
    # MEAN + RELIABILITY * (MAX_RATING - MEAN)
    adjusted_row <- .[2, ] + .[1, ] * (.[4, ] - .[2, ])
    bind_rows(., adjusted_row)
  }
```

```{r cor, eval = F, warning = F, results='asis'}
# determine vars
vars <- c(score_fft2, score_mqi, DVs_main)

# correlation and p values for raw
cor_raw <- psych::corr.test(
  df_teachers[, c(paste0(c(vars, DVs_supp)), "DAD_YRSEXP")]
)
p_raw <- matrix(p.adjust(cor_raw$p, method = "fdr"), nrow = ncol(cor_raw$p))
dimnames(p_raw) <- dimnames(cor_raw$p)

# correlation and p values for adj
cor_adj <- psych::corr.test(
  df_teachers[, c(paste0(c(vars, DVs_supp), "_adj"), "DAD_YRSEXP")]
)
p_adj <- matrix(p.adjust(cor_adj$p, method = "fdr"), nrow = ncol(cor_adj$p))
dimnames(p_adj) <- dimnames(cor_adj$p)

# function to format r and p values
fmt <- function(r, p){
  if( p < 0.001){
    paste0("r = ", fmt_nolead(r, 2), "\n(p <.001)")
  } else if( p == 1){
    paste0("r = ", fmt_nolead(r, 2), "\n(p = 1)")
  } else {
    paste0("r = ", fmt_nolead(r, 2), "\n(p = ", fmt_nolead(p, 3), ")")
  }
}

fmt_stars <- function(r, p){
  stars <- if( p < 0.001){
    "\n***"
  } else if( p < 0.01){
    "\n**"
  } else if( p < 0.05){
    "\n*"
  } else {
    ""
  }
  paste0(fmt_nolead(r, 2), stars)
}

# create combined matrices
n <- length(c(vars, DVs_supp, "DAD_YRSEXP"))
mat <- matrix("", n, n)
colnames(mat) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
rownames(mat) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
mat_stars <- matrix("", n, n)
colnames(mat_stars) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
rownames(mat_stars) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
r <- matrix(NA, n, n)
colnames(r) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
rownames(r) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
p <- matrix(NA, n, n)
colnames(p) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")
rownames(p) <- c(gsub("FFT_|MQI_|VA_", "", vars), "SAM(*)", "BAM(*)", "YRSEXP")


for (i in 1:n) {
  for (j in 1:n) {
    if(i < j){
      # Upper triangle: RAW
      mat[i, j] <- fmt(cor_raw$r[i, j], p_raw[i, j])
      mat_stars[i, j] <- fmt_stars(cor_raw$r[i, j], p_raw[i, j])
      r[i, j] <- cor_raw$r[i, j]
      p[i, j] <- p_raw[i, j]
    } else if(i > j){
      # Lower triangle: ADJ
      mat[i, j] <- fmt(cor_adj$r[i, j], p_adj[i, j])
      mat_stars[i, j] <- fmt_stars(cor_adj$r[i, j], p_adj[i, j])
      r[i, j] <- cor_adj$r[i, j]
      p[i, j] <- p_adj[i, j]
    } else { # use lower triangle too
      mat[i, j] <- fmt(cor_adj$r[i, j], p_adj[i, j])
      mat_stars[i, j] <- fmt_stars(cor_adj$r[i, j], p_adj[i, j])
      r[i, j] <- cor_adj$r[i, j]
      p[i, j] <- p_adj[i, j]
    }
  }
}
```

```{r nca, eval = F, warning = F}
# <<nca>> # make findable
test.rep = 100
test.rep = 10000

# initialise empty lists
list_ols <- list()
list_params <- list()
list_df_long <- list()
list_df_pred <- list()
list_df_abline <- list()
list_bottleneck <- list()

# standardise conditions and outcomes
# particularly important when outliers are removed
df_nca <- df_nca %>%
  mutate(
    across(all_of(c(conditions, vam)), ~scale(.x), .names = "{.col}_std")
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

for (v in 1:length(vam)) {
  
  measure = paste0(vam[v], "_std")
  
  # initialise empty vectors
  ols_intercept <- c()
  ols_slope <- c()
  nca_intercept <- c()
  nca_slope <- c()
  item <- c()
  outcome <- c()
  
  # MODEL 1: ONE PRED AT A TIME #
  
  for (c in 1:length(conditions)) {
    
    cond <- conditions[c]
    
    # run OLS - not standardised
    m <- lm(get(measure) ~ get(cond), data = df_nca)
    
    # extract intercept and slope
    ols_intercept <- c(ols_intercept, m$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]])
    ols_slope <- c(ols_slope, m$coefficients[["get(cond)"]])
    item <- c(item, cond)
    outcome <- c(outcome, measure)
    
    # extract coefs
    coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
    names(coef)[names(coef) == "Pr(>|t|)"] <- "p value"
    coef$Item <- gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", gsub("FFT_", "", cond))
    coef$Coefficient <- c("Intercept", "Beta")
    
    # extract model fit
    coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
    coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
    coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
    coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
    coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
    coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
    
    # combine coefs
    if (c == 1) adj <- coef else adj <- rbind(adj, coef)
    
    # define range of X for which to predict y values
    x_seq <- seq(xlim[1]-1, xlim[2]+1, length.out = 200)
    tmp <- data.frame(values = x_seq)
    names(tmp) <- cond
    # predict y values
    tmp <- as.data.frame(predict(m, newdata = tmp, interval = "confidence"))
    names(tmp)[1] <- "Score_y"
    tmp$y <- measure
    tmp$Test <- gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", gsub("VA_|VA_NOAGGR_", "", measure))
    tmp$Score_x <- x_seq
    tmp$x <- cond
    tmp$Item <- gsub("_adj", "", gsub("FFT_", "", cond))
    # combine
    if (v == 1 & c == 1) df_pred <- tmp else df_pred <- rbind(df_pred, tmp)
    
  }
  
  # process df_pred
  df_pred <- df_pred %>% 
    mutate(
      Item = factor(Item, levels = gsub("FFT_", "", gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", conditions))),
      Test = factor(Test, levels = c("SAM", "BAM"))
    )
  
  # store data in list
  list_df_pred[[measure]] <- df_pred
  
  for (c in 1:length(conditions)) {
    cond <- conditions[c]
    
    # run OLS - standardised
    m <- lm(get(measure) ~ scale(get(cond)), data = df_nca)
    
    # extract coefs
    coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
    names(coef)[names(coef) == "Pr(>|t|)"] <- "p value"
    coef$Item <- gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", gsub("FFT_", "", cond))
    coef$Coefficient <- c("Intercept", "Beta")
    # combine
    if (c == 1) adj_std <- coef else adj_std <- rbind(adj_std, coef)
  }
  
  # combine
  m1 <- left_join(adj %>% 
                    filter(Coefficient == "Beta") %>%
                    select(-Coefficient), 
                  adj_std %>% 
                    filter(Coefficient == "Beta") %>%
                    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate, SE_std = `Std. Error`) %>%
                    select(c(Item, Estimate_std, SE_std)), 
                  join_by(Item)
  ) %>%
    relocate(Item, Estimate, `Std. Error`, Estimate_std, SE_std) 
  
  # MODEL 2: ALL PRED TOGETHER #
  
  # run OLS - not standardised
  m <- lm(df_nca[, measure] ~ df_nca[, conditions[2]] + df_nca[, conditions[3]] + df_nca[, conditions[4]] + df_nca[, conditions[5]])
  adj <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  names(adj)[names(adj) == "Pr(>|t|)"] <- "p value"
  adj$Item <- gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", gsub("FFT_", "", c("", conditions[-1])))
  
  # extract model fit
  adj$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  adj$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
  adj$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
  adj$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
  adj$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
  adj$`p (F)` <- pf(adj$`F value`, adj$numdf, adj$dendf, lower.tail = F)
  
  # run OLS - standardised
  m <- lm(df_nca[, measure] ~ scale(df_nca[, conditions[2]]) + scale(df_nca[, conditions[3]]) + scale(df_nca[, conditions[4]]) + scale(df_nca[, conditions[5]]))
  adj_std <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  names(adj_std)[names(adj_std) == "Pr(>|t|)"] <- "p value"
  adj_std$Item <- gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", gsub("FFT_", "", c("", conditions[-1])))
  
  # combine
  m2 <- left_join(adj, 
                  adj_std %>% 
                    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate, SE_std = `Std. Error`) %>%
                    select(c(Item, Estimate_std, SE_std)), 
                  join_by(Item)
  ) %>%
    relocate(Item, Estimate, `Std. Error`, Estimate_std, SE_std) 
  
  # COMBINE MODELS
  ols <- left_join(m1, m2, join_by(Item)) %>%
    mutate(Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure)
  ols <- rbind(ols, NA)

  # store data in list
  list_ols[[measure]] <- ols
  
  
  # define NCA model - params will be extracted from here!
  invisible(capture.output(
    model <- nca_analysis(data = df_nca, 
                          x = conditions, 
                          y = measure, 
                          ceilings = ceilings,
                          test.rep = test.rep, # number of resamples in the statistical approximate permutation test
                          steps = seq(-4, 4, .5),
                          bottleneck.x = "actual",
                          bottleneck.y = "actual"
    )))
  
  # extract number of ceilings and conditions
  n_ceil <- length(model$bottlenecks)
  n_cond <- length(model$summaries)
  
  # save intercepts and slopes
  nca_intercept <- c(nca_intercept, unlist(model$Intercept))
  nca_slope <- c(nca_slope, unlist(model$Slope))
  
  # extract NCA params
  nca_param <- rbind(
    # combine model summary
    cbind(
      model$summaries[[1]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[2]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[3]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[4]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[5]]$global[, 1]
    ) %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      filter(!grepl("min|max", row.names(.))) 
    ,
    # combine NCA parameters
    cbind(
      model$summaries[[1]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[2]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[3]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[4]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[5]]$params[, 1:n_ceil]
    ) %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      filter(!grepl("# above", row.names(.))) 
  ) %>% 
    as.data.frame() 
  
  # add column names and unlist columns
  names(nca_param) <- conditions
  nca_param[, 1] <- as.numeric(c(nca_param[, 1]))
  nca_param[, 2] <- as.numeric(c(nca_param[, 2]))
  nca_param[, 3] <- as.numeric(c(nca_param[, 3]))
  nca_param[, 4] <- as.numeric(c(nca_param[, 4]))
  nca_param[, 5] <- as.numeric(c(nca_param[, 5]))
  
  # add outcome and stats as columns
  nca_param <- nca_param %>%
    mutate(
      Metric = row.names(.), 
      Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure, Metric)
  row.names(nca_param) <- NULL
  
  
  # create faceted plot for each indicator #
  
  # combine data for density plot
  df_nca_long <- df_nca %>%
    select(all_of(c(measure, conditions))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = conditions, names_to = "x", values_to = "Score_x") %>%
    mutate(
      y = measure,
      Score_y = .data[[measure]],
      x = factor(x, levels = conditions),
      fill_col = cols_obs[x]
    ) %>%
    select(-(.data[[measure]])) %>%
    # filter(x != conditions[1]) %>%
    mutate(Item = gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", x)) %>%
    left_join(., instrument_fft %>% 
                select(-Domain))  %>%
    mutate(
      Description = stringr::str_to_sentence(Description),
      Item = gsub("FFT_", "", Item),
      Item = factor(Item, levels = gsub("FFT_", "", gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", conditions))),
      Test = gsub("_adj_std", "", gsub("VA_|VA_NOAGGR_", "", y)),
      Test = factor(Test, levels = c("SAM", "BAM")),
      fill_vam = cols_vam[Test],
      fill_obs = cols_obs[gsub("_adj", "", x)]
    ) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  
  # store data in list
  list_df_long[[measure]] <- df_nca_long
  
  df_abline <- 
    # save CR intercepts and slopes
    data.frame(
      x = item,
      y = outcome,
      Test = outcome,
      cr_intercept = nca_intercept,
      cr_slope = nca_slope
    ) %>%
    # combine with OLS intercepts and slopes
    left_join(., data.frame(
      x = item,
      ols_intercept = ols_intercept,
      ols_slope = ols_slope)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Test = gsub("_adj_std", "", gsub("VA_|VA_NOAGGR_", "", Test)),
      Test = factor(Test, levels = c("SAM", "BAM"))
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      x = factor(x, levels = conditions),
      Item = gsub("FFT_", "", gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", x)),
      Item = factor(Item, levels = gsub("FFT_", "", gsub("_adj|_adj_std", "", conditions)))
    )
  
  # store data in list
  list_df_abline[[measure]] <- df_abline
  
  # --- BOTTLENECK TABLES --- #
  
  # bottleneck tables - actual values #
  
  # define NCA model
  invisible(capture.output(
    model <- nca_analysis(data = df_nca, 
                          x = conditions, 
                          y = measure, 
                          ceilings = ceilings,
                          steps = seq(-4, 4, .5),
                          bottleneck.x = "actual",
                          bottleneck.y = "actual"
    )))
  
  
  # extract bottleneck table
  tmp_act <- model$bottlenecks[[1]]
  for (i in 2:(n_cond+1)) {
    tmp_act[, i] <- c(model$bottlenecks[[1]][, i])
  }
  names(tmp_act)[-1] <- c(paste0(conditions, "_act"))
  
  # bottleneck tables - percentage range #
  
  # define NCA model
  invisible(capture.output(
    model <- nca_analysis(data = df_nca, 
                          x = conditions, 
                          y = measure, 
                          ceilings = ceilings,
                          steps = seq(-4, 4, .5),
                          bottleneck.x = "percentage.range",
                          bottleneck.y = "actual"
    )))
  
  # extract bottleneck table
  tmp_range <- model$bottlenecks[[1]]
  for (i in 2:(n_cond+1)) {
    tmp_range[, i] <- c(model$bottlenecks[[1]][, i])
  }
  names(tmp_range)[-1] <- c(paste0(conditions, "_range"))
  
  
  # bottleneck tables - percentiles #
  
  # define NCA model
  invisible(capture.output(
    model <- nca_analysis(data = df_nca, 
                          x = conditions, 
                          y = measure, 
                          ceilings = ceilings,
                          steps = seq(-4, 4, .5),
                          bottleneck.x = "percentile",
                          bottleneck.y = "actual"
    )))
  
  # extract bottleneck table
  tmp_perc <- model$bottlenecks[[1]]
  for (i in 2:(n_cond+1)) {
    tmp_perc[, i] <- c(model$bottlenecks[[1]][, i])
  }
  names(tmp_perc)[-1] <- c(paste0(conditions, "_perc"))
  
  # bottleneck tables - standardised values #
  
  tmp_conditions <- paste0(conditions, "_std")
  
  # define NCA model
  invisible(capture.output(
    model <- nca_analysis(data = df_nca, 
                          x = tmp_conditions, 
                          y = measure, 
                          ceilings = ceilings,
                          steps = seq(-4, 4, .5),
                          bottleneck.x = "actual",
                          bottleneck.y = "actual"
    )))
  
  # extract bottleneck table
  tmp_std <- model$bottlenecks[[1]]
  for (i in 2:(n_cond+1)) {
    tmp_std[, i] <- c(model$bottlenecks[[1]][, i])
  }
  
  names(tmp_std)[-1] <- c(paste0(tmp_conditions, "_act"))
  
  # combine bottlenecks for export #
  tmp <- tmp_act %>%
    left_join(tmp_std) %>%
    left_join(tmp_range) %>%
    left_join(tmp_perc) %>%
    rename(Outcome = paste(measure)) %>%
    mutate(Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure)
  
  # store data in list
  list_bottleneck[[measure]] <- tmp
  
  # extract NCA params from standardised model
  tmp_param <- rbind(
    # combine model summary
    cbind(
      model$summaries[[1]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[2]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[3]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[4]]$global[, 1],
      model$summaries[[5]]$global[, 1]
    ) %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      filter(grepl("Scope", row.names(.))) 
    ,
    # combine NCA parameters
    cbind(
      model$summaries[[1]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[2]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[3]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[4]]$params[, 1:n_ceil],
      model$summaries[[5]]$params[, 1:n_ceil]
    ) %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      filter(grepl("Ceiling zone|Slope|Intercept", row.names(.))) 
  ) %>% 
    as.data.frame() 
  
  # add column names and unlist columns
  names(tmp_param) <- tmp_conditions
  tmp_param[, 1] <- as.numeric(c(tmp_param[, 1]))
  tmp_param[, 2] <- as.numeric(c(tmp_param[, 2]))
  tmp_param[, 3] <- as.numeric(c(tmp_param[, 3]))
  tmp_param[, 4] <- as.numeric(c(tmp_param[, 4]))
  tmp_param[, 5] <- as.numeric(c(tmp_param[, 5]))
  
  # add outcome and stats as columns
  tmp_param <- tmp_param %>%
    mutate(
      Metric = row.names(.), 
      Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure, Metric)
  row.names(tmp_param) <- NULL
  
  # combine with params from using normal values
  nca_param <- left_join(nca_param, tmp_param)
  
  # clean up params
  nca_param <- left_join(build_nca_summary(nca_param, value_col = conditions[1]),  
                         build_nca_summary(nca_param, value_col = conditions[2]), join_by(Metric)) %>%
    left_join(., build_nca_summary(nca_param, value_col = conditions[3]), join_by(Metric)) %>%
    left_join(., build_nca_summary(nca_param, value_col = conditions[4]), join_by(Metric)) %>%
    left_join(., build_nca_summary(nca_param, value_col = conditions[5]), join_by(Metric)) %>%
    mutate(Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure, Metric) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  names(nca_param) <- c("Measure", "Metric", conditions)
  
  # store data in list
  list_params[[measure]] <- nca_param
  
}

# OLS table #

# Combine all OLS datasets
ols <- bind_rows(list_ols)

# create empty row
tmp <- list_ols[[paste0(vam, "_std")[1]]][1, ]
tmp[, 1:ncol(tmp)] <- NA

# combine both outcomes
ols <- tmp %>% 
  bind_rows(., tmp %>% mutate(Measure = paste0(vam, "_std")[1], Item = paste0(vam, "_std")[1])) %>%
  bind_rows(., list_ols[[paste0(vam, "_std")[1]]]) %>%
  bind_rows(., tmp %>% mutate(Measure = paste0(vam, "_std")[2], Item = paste0(vam, "_std")[2])) %>%
  bind_rows(., list_ols[[paste0(vam, "_std")[2]]]) %>%
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("t val"), ~sprintf("%.3f", .x)),
    across(starts_with("F val"), ~sprintf("%.3f", .x)),
    across(starts_with("p "), ~if_else(. < 0.001, "<.001", fmt_nolead(.x))),
    across(starts_with("R2"), ~if_else(!is.na(.x), paste0(fmt_nolead(.x*100, 2), "%"), NA)),
    across(starts_with("Esti"), ~sprintf("%.2f", .x)),
    across(starts_with("SE"), ~sprintf("%.2f", .x)),
    across(starts_with("Std."), ~sprintf("%.2f", .x)),
    across(everything(), ~gsub("NA", "", .x))
  )

# prepare for export
col_names1 <- c("", "", "Model 1", rep("", 11), "Model 2", rep("", 11))
col_names2 <- c("Outcome", "Observation score", rep(c("B", "SE_B", "β", "SE", "t", "p", "R2", "R2_adj", "F", "numdf", "dendf", "p (F)"), 2))
names(ols) <- col_names1
ols[1, ] <- col_names2


# save file
file_name <- paste0("coef_", file_name_stem, "_ols.csv")
write.csv(ols, file = file.path(dir_out, file_name), row.names = F)

# prepare for markdown
names(ols) <- col_names2
ols <- ols[-1, ]
idx <- which(is.na(ols$B))
idx <- which(ols$B == "")

# print to markdown
ols[-1] %>%
  kable(caption = "OLS coefficients", row.names = F, col.names = col_names2[-1]) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), fixed_thead = T, full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 1, "Model 1" = 12, "Model 2" = 12)) %>%
  row_spec(idx, bold = T) %>%
  add_footnote(c(paste0("Note. Data from ", nrow(df_nca), " teachers is included. In model 1, each predictor was entered seperately. In model 2, all predictors were entered together."),
                 paste0("This table was saved as ", file_name)), notation = "none") %>%
  print()

# NCA PARAMS # 

# Combine all param datasets
params <- bind_rows(list_params) 

# create empty row
tmp <- list_params[[paste0(vam, "_std")[1]]][1, ]
tmp[, 1:ncol(tmp)] <- NA

# combine both outcomes
params <- tmp %>% 
  mutate(Measure = paste0(vam, "_std")[1], Metric = paste0(vam, "_std")[1]) %>%
  bind_rows(., list_params[[paste0(vam, "_std")[1]]]) %>%
  bind_rows(., tmp %>% mutate(Measure = paste0(vam, "_std")[2], Metric = paste0(vam, "_std")[2])) %>%
  bind_rows(., list_params[[paste0(vam, "_std")[2]]]) 

# adjust p values
p <- as.numeric(params[params$Metric == "p value (unadj.)", conditions[1]])
params[params$Metric == "p value (adj.)", conditions[1]] <- fmt_nolead(p.adjust(p, method = "holm"))
params[params$Metric == "p value (unadj.)", conditions[1]] <- fmt_nolead(p)
p <- as.numeric(params[params$Metric == "p value (unadj.)" & params$Measure == paste0(vam, "_std")[1], conditions[-1]])
params[params$Metric == "p value (adj.)" & params$Measure == paste0(vam, "_std")[1], conditions[-1]] <- fmt_nolead(p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"))
params[params$Metric == "p value (unadj.)" & params$Measure == paste0(vam, "_std")[1], conditions[-1]] <- fmt_nolead(p)
p <- as.numeric(params[params$Metric == "p value (unadj.)" & params$Measure == paste0(vam, "_std")[2], conditions[-1]])
params[params$Metric == "p value (adj.)" & params$Measure == paste0(vam, "_std")[2], conditions[-1]] <- fmt_nolead(p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"))
params[params$Metric == "p value (unadj.)" & params$Measure == paste0(vam, "_std")[2], conditions[-1]] <- fmt_nolead(p)

# save file
file_name <- paste0("coef_", file_name_stem, "_nca.csv")
write.csv(params, file = file.path(dir_out, file_name), row.names = F)

# prepare for markdown
idx <- which(is.na(params[, 3]))

# print to markdown
params[-1] %>%
  kable(caption = "NCA parameters", row.names = F) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), fixed_thead = T, full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  row_spec(idx, bold = T) %>%
  add_footnote(c(paste0("Note. Data from ", nrow(df_nca), " teachers is included. NCA ceiling line = CR-FDH. Fit values of N/A indicate cases where the CR-FDH ceiling zone exceeds the CE-FDH ceiling zone, resulting in a negative closeness percentage that is not conceptually interpretable. This occurs when the straight-line CR-FDH approximation creates a larger empty space than the CE-FDH step-function boundary and does not invalidate effect sizes or ceiling accuracy."), paste0("p values were estimated using ", test.rep, " permutations."),
                 paste0("This table was saved as ", file_name)), notation = "none") %>%
  print()

  geom_abline(data = df_abline[df_abline$Item != "CEV" & df_abline$Test == "BAM", ], aes(slope = ols_slope, intercept = ols_intercept),

  geom_xsidehistogram(aes(fill = fill_obs), binwidth = xbin) +

  facet_wrap(vars(Item), nrow = 2) +
  ambition_theme +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(ylim[1]), ceiling(ylim[2]), ybreaks*2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(xlim[1]), ceiling(xlim[2]), xbreaks*2)) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  ylab(paste0(ylab)) + xlab(paste0(xlab)) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    ggside.axis.text = element_blank(),
    ggside.axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r regression, eval = F, warning = F}
# <<regression>> # make findable
# --- CONDITION INEFFCIENCY --- #

# initialise empty lists
list_ineff <- list()
list_inter <- list()

# use adjusted VAM but not standardised as all regression coefs will be standardised
vam <- VAM[grepl("adj", VAM)]
vam <- vam[!grepl("_NOAGGR_|_std", vam)]

for (v in 1:length(vam)) {
  
  measure = vam[v]
  
  cond <- "FFT_CEV_adj"
  # define NCA model
  invisible(capture.output(
    model <- nca_analysis(data = df_nca, 
                          x = cond, 
                          y = measure, 
                          ceilings = ceilings,
                          # test.rep = 10000, # number of resamples in the statistical approximate permutation test
                          steps = seq(-4, 4, .5),
                          bottleneck.x = "actual",
                          bottleneck.y = "actual"
    )))
  
  # extract ceiling line
  intercept <- model$plots[[1]]$lines$cr_fdh$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]]
  slope <- model$plots[[1]]$lines$cr_fdh$coefficients[["x"]]
  
  # extract bounding box
  xmin <- model$Xmin[[1]]
  xmax <- model$Xmax[[1]]
  ymin <- model$Ymin[[1]]
  ymax <- model$Ymax[[1]]
  
  # extract necessary condition zone (NCZ) boundaries
  y_cmin <- model$plots[[1]]$line_matrices$cr_fdh[2,2]
  x_cmax <- model$plots[[1]]$line_matrices$cr_fdh[3,1]
  
  # determine which observations lie in NCZ
  df_tmp <- df_nca
  df_tmp$below_ceil <- df_tmp[, measure] <= (intercept + slope * df_tmp[, cond]) # below or on the ceiling line
  df_tmp$ineff_outcome <- df_tmp[, measure] < y_cmin
  df_tmp$ineff_cond <- df_tmp[, cond] > x_cmax
  df_tmp$ncz <- df_tmp$below_ceil == T & df_tmp$ineff_outcome == F & df_tmp$ineff_cond == F
  df_tmp$ineff <- df_tmp$ineff_outcome == T | df_tmp$ineff_cond == T
  
  # plot data
  ggplot() +
    # bounding box
    geom_vline(xintercept = xmin, col = black40, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = xmax, col = black40, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ymin, col = black40, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ymax, col = black40, linetype = "dashed") +
    # NCZ box
    geom_vline(xintercept = x_cmax, col = red, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = y_cmin, col = blue, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    # ineff rectangles
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = x_cmax, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), alpha = 0.4, fill = red) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = y_cmin), alpha = 0.4, fill = blue) +
    # NCZ
    geom_polygon(data = data.frame(x = c(xmin, x_cmax, x_cmax), y = c(y_cmin, y_cmin, ymax)), aes(x=x, y=y), fill = teal, alpha = .4) +
    # scatterplot
    geom_point(data = df_tmp[df_tmp$below_ceil == F, ], aes(x = get(cond), y = get(measure)), col = black40) +
    geom_point(data = df_tmp[df_tmp$below_ceil == T & df_tmp$ncz == F, ], aes(x = get(cond), y = get(measure)), col = black) +
    geom_point(data = df_tmp[df_tmp$ncz == T, ], aes(x = get(cond), y = get(measure)), col = teal) +
    # ceiling line
    geom_abline(slope = slope, intercept = intercept, col = teal, linewidth = 1)
  
  
  # MODEL 1: ONE PRED AT A TIME, UNADJUSTED
  for (i in 1:length(score_mqi)) {
    # run OLS
    m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[, measure]) ~ 
              scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[i])]))
    # extract coefs
    coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
    # extract model fit
    coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
    coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
    coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
    coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
    coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
    coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
    
    # combine
    if (i == 1) out <- coef else out <- rbind(out, coef)
  }
  
  # process
  m1 <- out %>% 
    filter(! grepl("Intercept", rownames(.))) %>%
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model)
      ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:i)
  
  
  # MODEL 2: ONE PRED AT A TIME, ADJUSTED
  for (i in 1:length(score_mqi)) {
    # run OLS
    m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[, measure]) ~ 
              scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[i], "_adj")]))
    # extract coefs
    coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
    # extract model fit
    coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
    coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
    coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
    coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
    coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
    coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
    
    # combine
    if (i == 1) out <- coef else out <- rbind(out, coef)
  }
  
  # process
  m2 <- out %>% 
    filter(! grepl("Intercept", rownames(.))) %>%
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model)
      ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:i)
  
  
  # MODEL 3: ALL PREDS, ADJUSTED
  m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[, measure]) ~ 
            scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[1], "_adj")]) + 
            scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[2], "_adj")]) + 
            scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[3], "_adj")]) +
            scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[4], "_adj")]))
  
  # extract coefs
  coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  # extract model fit
  coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
  coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
  coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
  coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
  coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
  # process
  m3 <- coef %>% 
    filter(! grepl("Intercept", rownames(.))) %>%
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model)
      ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:i)
  
  
  # MODEL 4A: UNCONSTRAINED OBS (WITH COND INEFF)
  m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[df_tmp$ineff_cond, measure]) ~ 
            scale(df_tmp[df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[1], "_adj")]) + 
            scale(df_tmp[df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[2], "_adj")]) + 
            scale(df_tmp[df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[3], "_adj")]) +
            scale(df_tmp[df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[4], "_adj")]))
  # extract coefs
  coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  # extract model fit
  coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
  coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
  coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
  coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
  coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
  # process
  m4A <- coef %>% 
    filter(! grepl("Intercept", rownames(.))) %>%
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model)
      ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:i)
  
  # MODEL 4B: CONSTRAINED OBS (NO COND INEFF)
  m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[! df_tmp$ineff_cond, measure]) ~ 
            scale(df_tmp[! df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[1], "_adj")]) + 
            scale(df_tmp[! df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[2], "_adj")]) + 
            scale(df_tmp[! df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[3], "_adj")]) +
            scale(df_tmp[! df_tmp$ineff_cond, paste0(score_mqi[4], "_adj")]))
  # extract coefs
  coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  # extract model fit
  coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
  coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
  coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
  coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
  coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
  # process
  m4B <- coef %>% 
    filter(! grepl("Intercept", rownames(.))) %>%
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model)
      ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:i)
  
  # COMBINE MODELS
  ols <- left_join(m1, m2, join_by(Item)) %>%
    left_join(., m3, join_by(Item)) %>%
    left_join(., m4A, join_by(Item)) %>%
    left_join(., m4B, join_by(Item)) %>%
    mutate(Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure)
  ols <- rbind(ols, NA)

  # store data in list
  list_ineff[[measure]] <- ols
  
  # INTERACTION MODEL - DUMMY
  df_tmp$ineff_cond_dummy <- ifelse(df_tmp$ineff_cond == T, 0, # 0 if unconstrained
                                    ifelse(df_tmp$ineff_cond == F, 1, NA)) # 1 if constrained
  m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[, measure]) ~ 
            (scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[1], "_adj")]) + 
               scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[2], "_adj")]) + 
               scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[3], "_adj")]) +
               scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[4], "_adj")])) * df_tmp$ineff_cond_dummy)
  
  # extract coefs
  coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  # extract model fit
  coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
  coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
  coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
  coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
  coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
  
  # process
  m_dummy <- coef %>% 
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = c("Intercept", gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi), "Constraint", paste("Constraint x", gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi))),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model)
    ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:length(m$coefficients))
  
  
  # INTERACTION MODEL - EFFECT
  df_tmp$ineff_cond_effect <- ifelse(df_tmp$ineff_cond == T, -1, # -1 if unconstrained
                                     ifelse(df_tmp$ineff_cond == F, 1, NA)) # 1 if constrained
  m <- lm(scale(df_tmp[, measure]) ~ 
            (scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[1], "_adj")]) + 
               scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[2], "_adj")]) + 
               scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[3], "_adj")]) +
               scale(df_tmp[, paste0(score_mqi[4], "_adj")])) * df_tmp$ineff_cond_effect)
  
  # extract coefs
  coef <- as.data.frame(summary(m)$coefficients)
  # extract model fit
  coef$R2 <- summary(m)$r.squared
  coef$R2_adj <- summary(m)$adj.r.squared
  coef$`F value` <- summary(m)$fstatistic["value"]
  coef$numdf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["numdf"]
  coef$dendf <- summary(m)$fstatistic["dendf"]
  coef$`p (F)` <- pf(coef$`F value`, coef$numdf, coef$dendf, lower.tail = F)
  
  # process
  m_effect <- coef %>% 
    rename(Estimate_std = Estimate,
           `p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    mutate(
      Item = c("Intercept", gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi), "Constraint", paste("Constraint x", gsub("MQI_", "", score_mqi))),
      n_obs = nrow(m$model),
    ) %>% 
    relocate(Item, Estimate_std, `Std. Error`) %>%
    as.data.frame(row.names = 1:length(m$coefficients))
  
  
  # COMBINE MODELS
  ols <- left_join(m_dummy, m_effect, join_by(Item, n_obs)) %>%
    mutate(Measure = measure) %>%
    relocate(Measure)
  ols <- rbind(ols, NA)

  # store data in list
  list_inter[[measure]] <- ols
  
}

# OLS table - SUBGROUPS #

tmp <- list_ineff[[vam[1]]][1, ]
tmp[, 1:ncol(tmp)] <- NA

                 paste0("This table was saved as ", file_name)), notation = "none") %>%

                 "Following from the subgroup analysis, presence (CEV <= x_cmax) vs. absence (CEV > x_cmax) of a constraint of the condition on the outcome was included into the models as interaction term.", 
                 "In model 1, dummy coding was applied (0 = unconstrained, 1 = constrained). This places the unconstrained group as the reference group where the regression coefficient shows the difference between unconstrained and constrained. The intercept represents the value of the outcome in the unconstrained group when all predictors are 0. The MQI beta coefficients show the effects of each predictor in the unconstrained group. The constraint beta is the difference between the unconstrained and constrained group when all predictors are zero. The interaction terms show how the effect of each predictor changes in the constrained group relative to the unconstrained group.", 
                 "In model 2, effect coding was applied (-1 = unconstrained, 1 = constrained), hence the coefficients represent the difference between each group and the overall mean. The intercept represents the grand mean (average across both groups when all predictors are zero). The MQI beta coefficients show the average effect of each predictor across both groups. The constraint beta is the half the difference between the two groups when all predictors are zero. The interaction terms show half the difference in the effect of each predictor between the groups.",
                 paste0("This table was saved as ", file_name)), notation = "none") %>%
  print()
```

# Conditions: Framework for Teaching (FFT)  

FFT is an observational protocol designed to measure components of instruction that reflect a constructivist view of teaching. The instrument_fft was used in the MET Study to code instruction in all English and math classrooms at grades 4-9 using the domains "Classroom Environment" and "Instruction". Each of these domains, in turn, is measured by a number of indicators.  

- The domain *Classroom Environment* is measured along four indicators: creating an environment of respect and rapport; establishing a culture for learning; managing classroom procedures; and managing student behaviour.  
- The domain *Instruction* also is measured along four indicators: communicating with students; using questioning and discussion techniques, engaging students in learning, and using assessment in instruction.  

```{r, results='asis', message=F}
<<fft>>
```


FFT scoring is done using a detailed scoring rubric. However, unlike the other observation protocols used in the MET Study, raters use this rubric only once for each video, that is, a video scored with the FFT protocol will have only 1 score per video on each of the dimensions just described. In the MET Study, raters did not watch an entire video, however. Instead, raters watched for 15 minutes at the beginning of the video and then ten additional minutes at the 25-35 minute mark. They then scored the video as a single segment. Each indicator of the FFT protocol was scored on a 4-point scale ranging from unsatisfactory, to basic, to proficient, to distinguished, and for each indicator, a detailed scoring rubric described the kind of evidence appropriate for assigning a particular score. 

For each observer score $o$ at classroom section $k$ taught by teacher $j$ at time $t$, we estimated its reliability $\text{Reliability}_{ojkt}$ using the following formula: 

$$ 
\text{Reliability}_{ojkt} = \frac{\text{% teacher}}{\text{% teacher} + \frac{\text{% section}}{\text{# of sections}_{ojkt}} + \frac{\text{% lessons}}{\text{# of lessons}_{ojkt}} + \frac{\text{% raters}}{\text{# of raters}_{ojkt}} + \frac{\text{% residual}}{\text{total # of scores per teacher}_{ojkt}}} 
$$

Percentages ($\text{%}$) were based on the variance decomposition reported in Gates Foundation (2012) whereas counts ($\text{#}$) were derived based on the number of segments averaged.  

The reliability coefficients $\text{Reliability}_{ojkt}$ were then used to adjust observer score $o$ at classroom section $k$ taught by teacher $j$ at time $t$ towards the mean based on the reliability of each score using the following formula for reliability-based shrinkage:  

$$ 
\text{Score}_{adj, ojkt} = \overline{\text{Score}}_{ot} + \text{Reliability}_{ojkt} * (\text{Score}_{ojkt} - \overline{\text{Score}}_{ot}) 
$$



To better understand the results, we also standardised the adjusted observation scores.  
$$ 
\text{Score}_{adj, std, ojkt} = \frac{\text{Score}_{adj, ojkt} - \overline{\text{Score}}_{adj, ot}}{SD_{adj, ot}}
$$

# Predictors: Mathematical Quality of Instruction (MQI)  

MQI is an observational instrument designed to measure the mathematical work that occurs in classrooms, on the theory that such work is distinct from classroom climate, pedagogical style, or the deployment of generic instructional strategies. The MQI was used in the MET Study to code instruction in Mathematics at grades 4-9.  

The MQI instrument measures the mathematical quality of instruction by assessing classroom instruction along six domains: Richness of the Mathematics; Errors and Imprecision; Working with Students and Mathematics; Student Participation in Meaning-Making and Reasoning; Explicitness and Thoroughness; and Connections between Classroom Work and Mathematics.  

- The domain Richness of Mathematics captures student meaning making and classroom mathematical practices.  
- The domain Errors and Imprecision captures major errors made by the teacher, imprecision in language and notation used by the teacher, and lack of clarity.  
- The domain Working with Students and Mathematics captures how the teacher responds to students’ mathematical ideas and remediates student errors.  
- The domain Student Participation in Meaning-Making and Reasoning captures how students ask questions and reason about mathematics, students provide mathematical explanations, and the cognitive requirements of tasks.  
- The domain Explicitness and Thoroughness captures how complete the mathematical ideas and concepts are during the lesson.  
- The domain Connections between Classroom Work and Mathematics captures whether classroom activities are aimed at developing mathematical ideas.   

Note that of Connections between Classroom Work and Mathematics and Explicitness and Thoroughness, only one can apply depending on the content and grade level of the class where the other will be N/A. In Grades 4-7, raters judge Classroom Work and Mathematics and Explicitness and Thoroughness, whereas in Grade 9, raters judge Explicitness and Thoroughness. In Grade 8, there is a fairly even split. Any segments that had scores on either both of neither of the indicators were removed.

```{r, results='asis', message=F}
<<mqi>>
```

Raters score each segment on these indicators. MQI segment scoring was done by dividing the first 30 minutes of each video into 7.5 minute segments and then scoring each segment on the domains just described. The scoring rubric is built around a 3-point scale (domain not present, partially present, or predominantly present), and scoring anchors are provided for each score on each domain. In the MET Study, scores for each domain are often aggregated to higher levels of analysis simply by averaging raters’ scores to get a single segment score and then calculating the harmonic mean across segments for a particular target of measurement (e.g., a day, a class section, a teacher).  


# Outcomes: Value-added measures  

At grades 4-8, pupil learning was measured by state mathematics assessments as well as the Balanced Assessment in Mathematics (BAM) administered directly by MET researchers. BAM is an open ended assessment that seeks to measure pupils’ capacities in the following areas: modelling/formulating problems; transforming/manipulating mathematical formalisms; inferring/drawing conclusions; and communicating about mathematics. Each assessment form contains four to five assessment tasks and requires 50-60 minutes to complete. Concerns about generalisability led the MET researchers to administer three different forms of the BAM (from the relevant grade levels tests for 2003, 2004 and 2005) in each classroom. Thus, all pupils in a classroom (or class section) did not take the same test.  

MET researchers used pupil test scores to construct "value-added" measures of teaching effectiveness for individual teachers. The teachers provided information to indicate the percentage of instructional responsibility for all pupils in a MET classroom each time pupil data was collected. This information was connected with the pupil achievement data to estimate value-added measures of teaching effectiveness based on a single outcome (e.g., the state Mathematics test, or the BAM). MET researchers estimated value-added models for each outcome separately by grade and district, so that all value-added estimates are not just test-specific, but also grade and district specific. 

$$ 
Y_{sit} = X_{it}\beta + \overline{X}_{jkt}\gamma + \theta Z_{si(t-1)} + \lambda \overline{Z}_{sjk(t-1)} + \epsilon_{sit} 
$$

where:  
- $Y_{sit}$ is one of the achievement outcomes for pupil $i$ on test $s$ in the current school year $t$ (rank-based z-scores)  
- $X_{it}$ is a vector of pupil background variables for pupil $i$ at time $t$  
- $\overline{X}_{jkt}$ is a vector of the same pupil background variables, aggregated at section $k$ taught by teacher $j$ in which the pupil $i$ was enrolled at time $t$  
- $Z_{si(t-1)}$ is pupil $i$’s prior test score (in the same subject as test $s$) at year $t-1$  
- $\overline{Z}_{sjk(t-1)}$ is the prior test score (in the same subject as test $s$) at year $t-1$, aggregated at section $k$ taught by teacher $j$ in which the pupil $i$ was enrolled  
- $\epsilon_{sit}$ is a residual for pupil $i$ on test $s$ in year $t$  

There is also another set of value-added measures available that does not control for classroom-level aggregates:  

$$ Y_{sit} = X_{it}\beta + \theta Z_{si(t-1)} + \epsilon_{sit}$$

The residuals $\epsilon_{sit}$ were used as the basis for constructing value-added scores. The value-added score averages residuals  for test $s$ for the section $k$ taught by teacher $j$ in which the pupil $i$ was enrolled at time $t$.  Standard errors (SEs) for each teacher’s VAM are calculated as the SD of the residuals for a class section $k$ divided by the square root of the number of pupils residuals included in the classroom average.  

$$ 
\text{VAM}_{sjkt} =  \bar{\epsilon}_{sjkt} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i = 1}^{n}  \epsilon_{sit}
$$

$$
\text{SE}_{sjkt} = \frac{\text{SD}_{sjkt}}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (\epsilon_{sit} - \bar{\epsilon}_{sjkt}} )^2 }{\sqrt{n}}
$$

For each $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$, we estimated its reliability $\text{Reliability}_{sjkt}$ using the pooled variance $S^2_{pooled, st}$ of all $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$ and the error variance $\text{S}_{error, sjkt}^2$ of each $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$: 

$$ 
\text{Reliability}_{sjkt} = \frac{ S^2_{pooled, st} }{S^2_{pooled, st} + \text{S}_{error, sjkt}^2}
$$
The $S^2_{pooled, st}$ was computed as the variance across all classroom-level $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$ for test $s$ at time $t$. The $\text{S}_{error,  sjkt}^2$ was computed by squaring the $\text{SE}_{sjkt}$ reported for each $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$.   

$$
S^2_{pooled, st} = \frac{1}{m-1} \sum_{k=1}^{m} (\text{VAM}_{sjkt} - \overline{\text{VAM}}_{st})^2 
$$
where $\overline{\text{VAM}}_{st} = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{k=1}^{m}  \text{VAM}_{sjkt}$.

$$
\text{S}_{error, sjkt}^2 = \text{SE}_{sjkt}^2
$$




The reliability coefficients $\text{Reliability}_{sjkt}$ were then used to adjust the  $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$ towards the mean using the following formula for reliability-based shrinkage:  

$$ 
\text{VAM}_{adj, sjkt} = \overline{\text{VAM}}_{st} + \text{Reliability}_{sjkt} * (\overline{\text{VAM}}_{st} - \text{VAM}_{sjkt})
$$

To facilitate comparability, we standardised unadjusted and adjusted VAMs $\text{VAM}_{sjkt}$ and $\text{VAM}_{adj, sjkt}$ by subtracting the their means and dividing by their SD.  

$$ 
\text{VAM}_{std, sjkt} = \frac{\text{VAM}_{sjkt} - \overline{\text{VAM}}_{st}}{SD_{st}}
$$
$$ 
\text{VAM}_{adj, std, sjkt} = \frac{\text{VAM}_{adj, sjkt} - \overline{\text{VAM}}_{adj, st}}{SD_{adj, st}}
$$

# Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA)  

Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA: Dul, 2016) is a method to identify conditions that must be present for a particular outcome to occur, but alone may not be sufficient to guarantee that outcome. The focus is the determine whether the absence of a condition prevents the desired outcome, highlighting constraints rather than drivers of success.   

In traditional methods (e.g., multiple linear regression), it is assumed that each predictor additively influences the outcome. If one predictor is zero, the value of the outcome will be reduced unless the values of other predictors can compensate. In NCA, in comparison, the absence of a necessary condition results in outcome failure, independently of the value of the other predictors. Hence, in NCA, the aim is to search for empty areas in scatter plots between outcome and NCA predictor to draw a "ceiling line" to separate full and empty areas in the data. The presence of an empty zone is an indication of a necessary condition. This ceiling line marks the maximum possible value of the outcome for each value of the predictor to identify boundaries beyond which the outcome cannot go. In other words, a certain desired level of the outcome $Y = Y_C$ can only be achieved if $X \ge X_C$. This clearly differs from the concept of a regression line that shows the average relationship between two variables, typically by minimising the distance between the line and all data points.  

Scatter plots are the starting point for NCA where the potential necessary condition is plotted on the x axis against the outcome on the y axis. Then a ceiling line is drawn to separate the 'empty' (or ceiling) zone in the left corner from the 'full' zone. The aim is to make the ceiling zone as large as possible without allowing any observations in the ceiling zone above the ceiling line. However, this requires a trade-off between the size of the ceiling zone and the number of observations in the ceiling zone (referred to as outliers or exceptions).  

There are two classes of techniques to draw ceiling lines:  

- Ceiling envelopment (CE)  
- Ceiling regression (CR)  

**Ceiling envelopment (CE)** is a non-parametric technique. A piecewise linear or stepwise ceiling line is drawn by connecting the highest observed values of the outcome for each value of the potential necessary condition. The resulting line 'envelops' the data from above, showing the empirical limit of the outcome value for each value of the necessary condition. There are hence no observations above the ceiling line. The *CE Free Disposal Hull (FDH) method* forms the ceiling by connecting the highest outcome values with horizontal and vertical segments, resulting in stepwise linear boundaries. There are no restrictions on the shape of the line, allowing for abrupt changes and flat sections. It is hence flexible but sensitive to outliers. The *CE Varying returns to scale (VRS) method* uses the highest observed outcome values but connects them with straight lines to create piecewise linear convex boundaries. This allows the slope of the ceiling to change across intervals, reflecting the possibility that the relationship between necessary condition and outcome may vary at different levels. The CE-VRS method assumes that the ceiling line is convex. CE-VRS produces smoother lines compared to CE-FDH, accommodating varying returns to scale without assuming a fixed rate of change. However, CE-FDH does not require convexity of the ceiling function and is therefore preferred over CE-VRS as the default CE technique for NCA (Dul, 2016).  

**Ceiling regression (CR)** is a parametric technique. It fits a regression linear regression line through the points connecting the linear pieces of the CE ceiling line. The CR ceiling line is smooth and less sensitive to outliers compared the CE ceiling lines. The smoothing approach often leads to some observations in the ceiling zone as well as a smaller ceiling zone. CR methods introduce a parametric model to summarise the relationship between the necessary condition and outcome, while allowing for further modeling and comparison of ceiling lines. The *CR-FDH method* fits a regression model to the stepwise boundary formed by the CE-FDH approach. The *CR-VRS method* fits a regression model to the piecewise linear boundary formed by the CE-VRS approach. Similarly as above, CR-FDH is preferred over CR-VRS.  

Parameters of interest in NCA:  

- $\text{Scope} = (X_{max}-X_{min}) \times (Y_{max}-Y_{min})$ (empirical area of possible combinations between outcome and necessary condition, given the minimum and maximum observed values)  
- $\text{Ceiling zone}$ (size of the ceiling zone)  
- $\text{Effect size} = \frac{\text{Ceiling zone}}{\text{Scope}}\%$ (represents how much of a given value of the necessary condition constrains the outcome)  
- $\text{Accuracy of ceiling line} = \frac{N_{\text{Observations on or below the ceiling line}}}{N_{\text{Total observations}}} * 100\%$ (Benchmark is 95%)  
- $N_{\text{Observations above the ceiling line}}$  
- $\text{Fit}$ (closeness of the selected ceiling line to the CE-FDH line)  
- $\text{p value}$ (estimated using statistical approximate permutation tests, see Dul et al., 2020)  
- $\text{p accuracy}$ (estimated error of the p value, smaller error as number of resamples increases)  
- $\text{Slope}$ and $\text{Intercept}$ (parameters to describe straight ceiling line)
- $\text{Absolute inefficiency}$ (total xy-space where X does not constrain Y and Y is not constraint by X)  
- $\text{Relative inefficiency}$ (total xy-space where X does not constrain Y and Y is not constraint by X as percentage of $\text{Scope}$)  
- $\text{Condition inefficiency} = (X_{\text{High}}-X_{\text{cmax}}) / (X_{\text{High}}-X_{\text{Low}}) \times 100\%$ (range of X (as percentage of total range of X) where X does not constrain Y, i.e., percentage of X range where there is no ceiling line)  
- $\text{Outcome inefficiency} = (Y_{\text{cmin}}-Y_{\text{Low}}) / (Y_{\text{High}}-Y_{\text{Low}}) \times 100\%$ (range of Y (as percentage of total range of Y) where Y is not constraint by X, i.e., percentage of Y range where there is no ceiling line)  

The bottleneck table shows which level of the necessary condition is necessary for each level of outcome. For a given outcome value, it shows the minimum required values of the independent variables.
